Hi Logan,

Thanks for sending. Procurement looped me in — we have a few compliance and procurement checkpoints before we can accept on-prem deployments or deep discounts:

1) Export controls / restricted end-use questionnaire completed and reviewed. We need to confirm you can support export screening and audit logs.
2) SOC 2 / ISO artifacts and data residency guarantees (we operate globally and have customers in regulated industries).
3) Confirmation that your platform will not enable downstream export of models or weights without our prior approval.

Can you share the export questionnaire and the SOC 2 report? Also, we need to confirm whether any Sunridge subsidiaries operate in countries with restricted trade lists — that may affect final approval.

Logan — thanks for flagging.

Initial Deal Desk take: 30% exceeds standard introductory limits for this segment; our delegated authority caps at 15% for AE approvals and 20% for regional managers with justification. Anything above 20% requires VP/exec sign-off.

Separately, the on-prem/private deployment is a material operational exception — requires Security & Compliance sign-off plus additional contractual protections (export controls addendum, audit rights, KYC).

Neha — can you run an eligibility screen? Prioritise: export control list check, sanctions screening on ultimate parent and subsidiaries, and any red flags in customer vertical (Sunridge works in specialized edge compute for industrial robotics — potential dual-use).

Notes: attaching our standard export questionnaire for Sunridge to complete, and linking the HubSpot deal.

Subject: RE: Fwd: Redwood proposal + ask on on-prem & discount — Sunridge (Deal: DEAL-2027-2137)

Team — I completed an initial eligibility review this morning. Summary of findings: 

1) Sanctions & export screening: Sunridge HQ is in the US (CA). However, one operational subsidiary (Sunridge Systems Asia Pte Ltd) is incorporated in Singapore with business units that resell into APAC markets including customers in Southeast Asia and the Middle East. Public records show a historic customer in a defense-adjacent OEM in 2019 (no sanctions record), which flags this as "dual-use" risk. No OFAC or EU sanctions listings for the parent or subsidiaries at this time.

2) KYC/customer footprint: corporate ownership appears clean based on open-source checks, but we need completed questionnaires (they are missing a line-item about end-customer use cases) and proof of business registration for subsidiaries.

3) Risk recommendation: allow conditional approval with constraints — do NOT approve the full 30% introductory discount. Proposed safe path: approve up to 20% discount contingent on: signed export-controls addendum, documented proof that Sunridge will not use outputs/models for restricted military end uses, and successful completion of a basic site/partner screening for the Asia subsidiary. Also require operational controls: audited access logs, restricted model export flags, and a monthly compliance report for the first 6 months.

Attachments: eligibility_findings_summary.docx

If Sales and Deal Desk want a larger concession (>=25%), this needs VP-level approval with Legal-signed indemnities and possibly a holdback on SLA for certain use-cases. Recommend looping Marissa for executive sign-off on the exception.

Neha Kapoor
Head of Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference

Thanks for the diligence everyone. After reviewing Neha's findings and Deal Desk constraints, approved exception as follows: 

- Commercial: one-time 20% introductory discount for first 12 months (approved). Any additional discount requires VP approval.
- Deployment: private/dedicated footprint in us-west only. On-prem will not be allowed at this time; we will provide VPC + private key integration.
- Controls required before go-live: executed export-controls addendum, signed non-export use clause, proof of subsidiary registrations, and a compliance onboarding checklist (logs/audit access enabled).

Action items:
1) Lauren (Legal) — work with Sunridge to insert the export addendum and non-export clause; include audit rights and indemnity language as discussed.
2) Karthik/Finance — update quote to reflect the approved 20% discount and finalize billing terms.
3) Logan — communicate approved commercial terms and constraints to the customer and schedule a follow-up with Procurement to finish paperwork.
4) Neha/Trust — run the partner/subsidiary screening and confirm before provisioning.

Logan — please reply-all to confirm you'll proceed under these constraints. Once Legal posts the redlined SOW, we'll route for signatures.
